observation.visible_scene: A person stands on a grassy cliff edge with their back mostly to the camera, arms stretched out sideways holding the top corners of a white banner printed with the five Olympic rings. Beyond them a wide calm river runs across the frame, backed by a dense forested strip and marshy water under a low sun in the upper-left that throws a bright glare and reflection onto the water. The sky is clear and pale blue.
visible_changes: The banner is held horizontally spread at the start, then its fabric ripples and folds: the right half bunches and curls forward over the center (frames ~2-8), the cloth progressively collapses into a narrower diagonal/vertical sheet wrapped around the person's body (frames ~9-24), and finally re-opens back into a broad rectangular spread held by both corners (frames ~28-41).

The person's torso and head rotate slightly during the middle of the clip (a small turn toward their right) and then return to a back-facing stance as the banner re-extends; the feet remain planted on the same spot on the ridge.

The sun position, its water reflection, the tree line and the horizon stay essentially unchanged throughout, indicating the background is static while the banner and the person's upper body are what move.
The banner's ring pattern remains visible but is repeatedly distorted, partially hidden, and re-oriented by the folding cloth rather than by the rings themselves moving.
outside_clip_unknowns: What drives the folding (wind gusts versus the person's own arm/hand movements) is not established within the excerpt.
Whether the person's slight turn is an intentional repositioning of the banner or a reaction to the cloth is unseen.
The state of the banner before t=0 and after the last frame is unknown; the clip is a middle segment and the spread-fold-spread pattern may continue or repeat outside it.
uncertain_details: Possible very small camera drift or tilt (the person's feet sit a little lower in the frame near the end), but the fixed sun and horizon make any camera motion minimal and not clearly separable from the subject's own movement.
Exact handedness of the banner's corners and whether we view the front or mirrored back of the rings is ambiguous due to the folds and lighting.
The person's head orientation in the middle frames is partly occluded by the banner, so the degree of body rotation is approximate.
